v3.title: v3 · truth fixes
v3.summary: v2 with the statements the outside review found untrue or misleading corrected. Nothing new is added except the Whitworth half-turn times, which replace a misleading fact.
changes: “Turn together, so they stay parallel” now says only that the angle between them never changes, and names a parallel pair of lines only when there is one (wiper: P-T stays parallel to Q-U).
A body that keeps its orientation says whether it moves in a straight line or along an arc (wiper CD: curvilinear translation, not a straight line; Scotch yoke CD: straight line).

A pin sliding in a moving slot no longer gets stroke times; that “3 s and 3 s” is what made Luna say the Whitworth has no quick return. The slotted link now gives its slow and fast half-turn times (3.65 s vs 2.35 s).
“Nearly straight for X% of the cycle” is measured in time, counting both passes of a back-and-forth path (Chebyshev 46% → 92%).
A parallelogram is checked against the coupler actually keeping its angle; a crossed one would be called an antiparallelogram.
Dropped two unproven causes: “because the input is not at its pivot” and “when one end rises the other falls” (now: the ends move in opposite directions).
A drawing the solver cannot solve is described as unsolved as drawn, not as a mechanism that cannot move (no template here hits this).

v4.title: v4 · jobs, family check, schematic filmstrip
v4.summary: The app does more of the reasoning and says it in the app's words; the picture is the app's own Schematic drawing at four moments; the prompt asks for a glossary with meanings and for the specific machine the mechanism resembles.
changes: Links and their jobs: every link is named for its job (input crank, coupler, rocker, beam, slotted link, yoke, connecting rod, slider), and each rocker's and slider's two ends are keyed to the input's angle, e.g. “reaches its ends when link AB is at 26 deg and 192 deg”. The same list is the panel's Links table.

Family check: PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog (crank-rocker and the other Grashof classes, parallelogram, slider-crank, Scotch yoke, Whitworth and slotted-lever quick returns, Chebyshev, Roberts, Hoeken and Watt straight-line linkages, Jansen, walking beam, crank-rocker driving a parallelogram, cylinder-driven lever) and names the chain type (Watt or Stephenson six-bar). The note may say “This mechanism is a …” only for a match.

The picture is the app's Schematic style, captured from the drawing-styles build at four moments (a full turn's quarters, or a back-and-forth's two ends and two points between), with authored link names hidden because they give the answer away (“Wiper arm”, “Hood”).
The sheet leads with what matters (at a glance, family, jobs) and puts coordinates last; long per-body length lists are trimmed to the lengths between connecting joints.
“This mechanism” throughout, in the sheet and in the note; the note never mentions the fact sheet or the picture.
Terms come with a meaning, which the panel shows on hover; uses may be fewer than two, and should be what the type is best known for.
After the app's family, the note names the specific machine it strongly resembles, if any: “a Stephenson six-bar that resembles a car hood hinge”.

pairs.name: Four-Bar
pairs.blurb: A classic crank-rocker: a crank turns, a rocker swings, and the coupler between them draws a curve.

answer.plainEnglish: This is a crank-rocker four-bar. **AB** makes full turns about fixed joint **A**, carrying **B** around a circle. **BC** connects the crank to **CD** and rocks as the floating coupler changes angle; **CD** swings back and forth about fixed joint **D**. In this drawing, **BC** rocks through 63.4 degrees, while **CD** rocks through a wider 107.9 degrees, turning the continuous input into an oscillating output.

useCases.why: The full-turn crank and rocking output link suit driving a wiper back and forth.
The oscillating output link can move a screen repeatedly through an arc.

### Structure
- Rigid bodies (moving links): 3.

- link BC lengths: B-C 5.75.
- link CD lengths: C-D 3.74.
### Input
- rotary drive at joint A, turning link AB relative to the ground; speed 10 rpm clockwise.
### Solved motion
- Degrees of freedom: 1. Solved 361 samples over 6 s.
- The input runs continuously; the whole motion repeats once per input revolution.
- link AB turns full revolutions about ground pivot A, at a steady angular speed.
- link BC rocks (no fixed pivot: a floating coupler) through 63.4 deg (from 5.9 to 69.4 deg); one way takes 3.53 s and the other 2.47 s (time ratio 1.43).
- link CD rocks about ground pivot D through 107.9 deg (from -111 to -3.1 deg); one way takes 3.23 s and the other 2.77 s (time ratio 1.17).

answer.plainEnglish: This is a crank-rocker four-bar: the driven **AB** makes full turns around fixed joint **A**, carrying floating link **BC** through the loop. That motion makes **CD** swing back and forth around fixed joint **D**. In this drawing, the ground pivots **A** and **D** are 6.48 cm apart. The two moving bars therefore have different jobs: **AB** keeps rotating, while **BC** transfers motion to the rocking output **CD**.

useCases.why: A continuously rotating input can drive an output link that swings back and forth, as **CD** does here.
The rotating **AB** and rocking **CD** show how a four-bar can convert continuous rotation into a repeated swing.

pairs.name: Slider-Crank
pairs.blurb: Rotation into a straight push — the engine and the pump both live here.

answer.plainEnglish: This is an offset slider-crank. **AB** rotates fully around fixed joint **A**, carrying **B** in a circle; rod **BC** connects **B** to slider **C** and makes it move back and forth along its guide. The guide is offset from **A**, so the two strokes take different times: in this drawing’s motion, the slider’s return takes 3.3 seconds and the other stroke takes 2.7 seconds. The coupler **BC** rocks as it transmits the crank’s rotation to the slider.

useCases.why: The slider’s back-and-forth travel can drive a pump piston.
A slider-crank connects a rotating crank to a piston moving back and forth.
The slider’s reversing travel can move a compressor piston.

pairs.name: Whitworth Quick-Return
pairs.blurb: Crank longer than the ground offset, so the lever turns instead of rocking.

diff.line: - Pin B slides 2 back and forth within the slot on link CD; this is motion relative to link CD, not an output stroke.
- Slider B travels 2 along its guide on link CD; one way takes 3 s and the other 3 s (time ratio 1).

- link AB (radius 3 about A) drives link CD through pin B riding in a slot on link CD, which pivots at C, 1 from A. The crank radius is larger than that pivot distance, so link CD turns fully but unevenly (the rotating-slotted-link arrangement). Its slowest half-turn takes 3.65 s and the opposite half-turn 2.35 s (time ratio 1.55), so anything it drives back and forth through those two half-turns gets a slow stroke and a quick return.

- link AB (radius 3 about A) drives link CD through pin B riding in a slot on link CD, which pivots at C, 1 from A. The crank radius is larger than that pivot distance, so link CD turns fully but unevenly, fast on one half-turn and slow on the other (the rotating-slotted-link arrangement).

answer.plainEnglish: This resembles a Whitworth quick-return mechanism. **AB** is the input crank, turning steadily around fixed joint **A**. Its pin **B** rides in the slot of **CD**, making **CD** pivot around fixed joint **C** and turn through full revolutions at a changing speed. In this drawing, **A** and **C** are 1 cm apart, and the two slider directions each take 3 seconds, so the motion has no faster return stroke.

useCases.why: A rotating-slotted-link arrangement can provide a slower cutting stroke and a quicker return, though this fact sheet shows equal times in both directions.
The rotating slotted link converts steady crank rotation into reciprocating motion, as shown by **B** sliding along **CD**.

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: the cylinder between I and E, which extends and retracts at 0.2 cm/s.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The input runs to a limit and reverses, so every part moves back and forth; one full back-and-forth takes 9.15 s.
- Traced points: B (on link ABHKLMNOPQ). The author chose to show these paths, so they are probably the outputs this mechanism exists for.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 4 links counting the ground, joined by 4 pin joints (the cylinder that drives it not counted): a single four-bar loop.
- Matches: triple-rocker four-bar. Non-Grashof: shortest + longest 2.98 vs the other two 2.72.
- Also matches: cylinder-driven lever. Cylinder I-E, anchored at I, pushes link EJG at E and swings it about its fixed pivot.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots I, J, A (apart: I-J 2.2; I-A 0.34; J-A 2.1).

### At a glance
- Driven input: the cylinder between A and D, which extends and retracts at 1 cm/s.

### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 4 links counting the ground, joined by 3 pin joints and 2 sliding joints (the cylinder that drives it not counted).
- Matches: cylinder-driven lever. Cylinder A-D, anchored at A, pushes link GDMK at D and swings it about its fixed pivot.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots A, G (apart: A-G 10).
- link GDMK — rocker: rocks about ground G through 40.5 deg; it reaches its two ends when cylinder A-D's length is 4.54 and 8.34; the cylinder pushes it at D.
- link SMT — connecting rod: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 40.5 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link TU — yoke (carries the slot): slides in a straight line at 90 deg without turning, moving 8.95 back and forth (straight-line translation).
- pin K — pin in a slot: slides 6.53 back and forth within the slot on link TU (motion relative to that link, not an output stroke).
- slider S — slider on a fixed guide: travels 6.53 back and forth along a fixed guide at 0 deg; it reaches its two ends when cylinder A-D's length is 8.34 and 4.54.
- cylinder A-D — driven input (a linear actuator); the block marked C on it is the cylinder's own sliding seal, part of the cylinder and not a separate slider: extends and retracts between lengths 4.54 and 8.34 (travel 3.8).

- Slider-crank arrangement driven by a rocking lever: link GDMK (arm 8 from its pivot G, swinging 40.5 deg) pushes slider S along its guide through rod link SMT (length 8).

- The cylinder pushes link GDMK at D, 6 from its pivot G: 3.8 of extension swings it 40.5 deg, about 10.6 deg per unit of extension.

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint K turns link KP relative to link HK at 4 rpm clockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The input runs to a limit and reverses, so every part moves back and forth; one full back-and-forth takes 5.5 s.
- Traced points: P (on link KP). The author chose to show these paths, so they are probably the outputs this mechanism exists for.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 4 links counting the ground, joined by 4 pin joints: a single four-bar loop.
- Matches: crank-rocker four-bar. Grashof, link BP is shortest: shortest + longest 7.69 vs the other two 8.6.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots H, B (apart: H-B 5.99).
- link HK — rocker: rocks about ground H through 42.9 deg; it reaches its two ends when link KP's angle (K to P) is 259 deg and 244 deg.
- link KP — input link (driven at K): has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 30.7 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link BP — rocker, carries traced point P: rocks about ground B through 163.2 deg; it reaches its two ends when link KP's angle (K to P) is 259 deg and 232 deg.
### How the parts relate
- Four-bar loop: link HK (H-K) 4.2, link KP (K-P) 4.4, link BP (B-P) 1.7, ground H-B 5.99. It is a Grashof crank-rocker: link BP (B-P) is the shortest bar, so it is able to turn fully while the opposite side bar only rocks (shortest + longest = 7.69 vs the other two = 8.6). In this mechanism it does not turn fully: it sweeps 163.2 deg over the solved motion.
- P's path lies overlapping the span of the ground pivots (path x -0.05 to 1.7, y -1.61 to 1.7; pivots x -1.5 to 0, y 0 to 5.8).
### Paths of moving points
- K: circular arc of radius 4.2 about H, sweeping 42.9 deg back and forth.
- P (traced): circular arc of radius 1.7 about B, sweeping 163.2 deg back and forth.

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint A turns link AB relative to the ground at 10 rpm clockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The motion repeats every 6 s, once per input revolution.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 3 links counting the ground, joined by 1 pin joint and 2 sliding joints.
- Matches: Scotch yoke. Link AB turns fully and its pin B rides a slot in link CDE, which slides without turning.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots A.
- link AB — input crank: turns full revolutions about ground A, at a steady angular speed.
- link CDE — yoke (carries the slot): slides in a straight line at 0 deg without turning, moving 2 back and forth (straight-line translation).
- pin B — pin in a slot: slides 2 back and forth within the slot on link CDE (motion relative to that link, not an output stroke).
- slider C — slider on a fixed guide: travels 2 back and forth along a fixed guide at 0 deg; it reaches its two ends when link AB's angle (A to B) is 180 deg and 0 deg; one way takes 3 s and the other 3 s (time ratio 1).
### How the parts relate
- link AB (radius 1 about A) drives link CDE through pin B riding in a slot on link CDE. link CDE cannot turn, so it follows only the part of B's circular motion along its own guide: a steady crank gives it a smooth back-and-forth (harmonic) motion.

- C: straight line at 0 deg, length 2 (back and forth).

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint O turns link OAR relative to the ground at 10 rpm counterclockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The motion repeats every 6 s, once per input revolution.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 5 links counting the ground, joined by 5 pin joints and 1 sliding joint.
- Matches: in-line slider-crank. Link OAR turns fully and drives slider C along a fixed guide through connecting rod link AC.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots O, P (apart: O-P 4).
- link OAR — input crank: turns full revolutions about ground O, at a steady angular speed.
- link AB — translating link: moves along a curve without turning: not in a straight line; every point of it traces the same circular arc as A (radius 0.8 about O), shifted (curvilinear translation).
- link PBS — crank: turns full revolutions about ground P, at a steady angular speed.
- link AC — connecting rod: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 18.2 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- slider C — slider on a fixed guide: travels 1.6 back and forth along a fixed guide at 0 deg; it reaches its two ends when link OAR's angle (O to R) is 0 deg and 180 deg; one way takes 3 s and the other 3 s (time ratio 1).
### How the parts relate
- Four-bar loop: link OAR (O-A) 0.8, link AB (A-B) 4, link PBS (P-B) 0.8, ground O-P 4. It is a parallelogram: opposite bars are equal and the coupler keeps its angle, so the coupler stays parallel to the ground line and the two side bars stay parallel to each other.
- Slider-crank: link OAR (radius 0.8 about O) drives slider C through rod link AC (length 5.06, 6.33x the crank radius). The guide is in line with the crank pivot, so the two strokes are symmetric.
- link OAR and link PBS turn together: their angles change identically at every instant (both sweep 360 deg), so the angle between them never changes. Line O-R stays parallel to line P-S.
- link OAR is a lever (beam) pivoted at O between A and R: they sit on opposite sides of the pivot (arms 0.8 and 1.6), so the two ends always move in opposite directions, and R moves 2x as far as A.
- link PBS is a lever (beam) pivoted at P between B and S: they sit on opposite sides of the pivot (arms 0.8 and 1.6), so the two ends always move in opposite directions, and S moves 2x as far as B.
### Paths of moving points
- A: full circle of radius 0.8 about O.
- R: full circle of radius 1.6 about O.
- B: full circle of radius 0.8 about P.
- S: full circle of radius 1.6 about P.
- C: straight line at 0 deg, length 1.6 (back and forth).

rounds.note: The first round asked blind. Until now the picture reached the model under a file name that was the template's own (cases/Bell_Crank.filmstrip.png), and Codex shows the model that path; from here the picture is sent as picture.png. Twelve library templates (eight never used), eight student mechanisms and one test case. Both sides are each version's first blind asking; both were asked five times blind, and five times with the old file names, to measure the difference.

Offset_Mount_Hatch.why: v7 says a powered vehicle hatch in all five askings, from the names its author gave the parts ("Hatch", "Offset barrel", "Rod bracket"); v6, without them, says a cylinder-operated swinging arm and names an excavator boom.

Crane_Two_Loads.why: v7 says a crane jib luffing mechanism in all five askings, from the names "Jib", "Luffing crank" and "Luffing link"; v6 says a quick-return lever drive and names a shaper (none of its five askings says crane).

Pumping_Field.why: v7 says a walking-beam pump jack; v6's first asking names no resemblance and no use (its other four say a pump jack, as the app's walking-beam match suggests).

student-196f7ddefeb9.why: v6 puts no part name in bold, so the panel cannot point at any, and calls the stuck drawing a pair of linked slotted levers; v7 describes it and claims nothing.

Hood_Hinge.why: Both "Looks like" lines are wrong: v6 a powered lifting gate, v7 a tractor front loader, though v7's paragraph calls the long link by its author's name, Hood, and two of its other four askings say a car hood. v6 never does in five.

Aircraft_Landing_Gear.why: Neither sees landing gear in any of ten blind askings. v6, with the photograph at full strength, says a helicopter rotor linkage every time (it sees the propeller); v7, with it faded, wanders: wipers, a mower deck, a window shade.

Excavator_Bucket.why: Both say a reciprocating pump linkage; each names an excavator in two of its five askings.

Car_Steering.why: Neither sees steering in any of ten blind askings: twin rockers, wipers, pump beams.

student-added-steam-.why: Neither sees a locomotive: v6 three synchronized cranks, v7 rotating display wheels, which nothing suggests.

made-locomotive-wheels.why: Neither sees locomotive wheels in any of ten blind askings. The "locomotive wheel drive" of round 4 came with the file name made-locomotive-wheels.

answer.plainEnglish: This mechanism turns the input at **C** into a rocking motion of **CDE** about **D**. ### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots A, D (apart: A-D 4.2).
- link AB — rocker: rocks about ground A through 155.2 deg; it reaches its two ends when link CDE's angle (C to E) is 21 deg and 345 deg.
- link BC — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 28.5 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link CDE — input rocker (driven back and forth): rocks about ground D through 37.8 deg.
- link EF — connecting rod: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 5.3 deg while it moves (general plane motion).

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint A turns link AB relative to the ground at 10 rpm clockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The motion repeats every 6 s, once per input revolution.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 6 links counting the ground, joined by 7 pin joints: a six-bar chain of the Watt type, because its two three-joint links (the ground and link CDE) are joined directly.
- Matches: Watt six-bar. Its two three-joint links are joined directly.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots A, D, G (apart: A-D 4.61; A-G 8.12; D-G 3.52).
- link AB — input crank: turns full revolutions about ground A, at a steady angular speed.
- link BC — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 29.4 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link CDE — rocker: rocks about ground D through 61 deg; it reaches its two ends when link AB's angle (A to B) is 36 deg and 211 deg; one way takes 3.08 s and the other 2.92 s (time ratio 1.06).
- link EF — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 30.8 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link FG — rocker: rocks about ground G through 42.3 deg; it reaches its two ends when link AB's angle (A to B) is 356 deg and 211 deg; one way takes 2.42 s and the other 3.58 s (time ratio 1.48).
### How the parts relate
- Four-bar loop: link AB (A-B) 1, link BC (B-C) 4, link CDE (D-C) 2, ground A-D 4.61. It is a Grashof crank-rocker: link AB (A-B) is the shortest bar, so it is able to turn fully while the opposite side bar only rocks (shortest + longest = 5.61 vs the other two = 6).

- E: circular arc of radius 1.6 about D, sweeping 61 deg back and forth.
- F: circular arc of radius 1.2 about G, sweeping 42.3 deg back and forth.

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint O turns link OAR relative to the ground at 10 rpm counterclockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The motion repeats every 6 s, once per input revolution.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 5 links counting the ground, joined by 5 pin joints and 1 sliding joint.
- Matches: in-line slider-crank. Link OAR turns fully and drives slider C along a fixed guide through connecting rod link AC.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots O, P (apart: O-P 4).
- link OAR — input crank, drawn by its author as a disc (a wheel or flywheel): turns full revolutions about ground O, at a steady angular speed.
- link AB — translating link: moves along a curve without turning: not in a straight line; every point of it traces the same circular arc as A (radius 0.8 about O), shifted (curvilinear translation).
- link PBS — crank, drawn by its author as a disc (a wheel or flywheel): turns full revolutions about ground P, at a steady angular speed.
- link AC — connecting rod: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 18.2 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- slider C — slider on a fixed guide: travels 1.6 back and forth along a fixed guide at 0 deg; it reaches its two ends when link OAR's angle (O to R) is 0 deg and 180 deg; one way takes 3 s and the other 3 s (time ratio 1).
### How the parts relate
- Four-bar loop: link OAR (O-A) 0.8, link AB (A-B) 4, link PBS (P-B) 0.8, ground O-P 4. It is a parallelogram: opposite bars are equal and the coupler keeps its angle, so the coupler stays parallel to the ground line and the two side bars stay parallel to each other.
- Slider-crank: link OAR (radius 0.8 about O) drives slider C through rod link AC (length 5.06, 6.33x the crank radius). The guide is in line with the crank pivot, so the two strokes are symmetric.
- link OAR and link PBS turn together: their angles change identically at every instant (both sweep 360 deg), so the angle between them never changes. Line O-R stays parallel to line P-S.
- link OAR is a lever (beam) pivoted at O between A and R: they sit on opposite sides of the pivot (arms 0.8 and 1.6), so the two ends always move in opposite directions, and R moves 2x as far as A.
- link PBS is a lever (beam) pivoted at P between B and S: they sit on opposite sides of the pivot (arms 0.8 and 1.6), so the two ends always move in opposite directions, and S moves 2x as far as B.
### Paths of moving points
- A: full circle of radius 0.8 about O.
- R: full circle of radius 1.6 about O.
- B: full circle of radius 0.8 about P.
- S: full circle of radius 1.6 about P.
- C: straight line at 0 deg, length 1.6 (back and forth).
### The picture: this mechanism at six moments, numbered in time order
- 1: 0 s, link OAR's angle (O to R) 270 deg.
- 2: 1 s, link OAR's angle (O to R) 330 deg.
- 3: 2 s, link OAR's angle (O to R) 30 deg.
- 4: 3 s, link OAR's angle (O to R) 90 deg.
- 5: 4 s, link OAR's angle (O to R) 150 deg.
- 6: 5 s, link OAR's angle (O to R) 210 deg.
### Geometry at the start, for reference
- Joints: O (0, 0) ground; A (0, 0.8); R (0, -1.6); B (4, 0.8); P (4, 0) ground; S (4, -1.6); C (-5, 0) slider.
- link OAR: O-A 0.8; O-R 1.6; A-R 2.4.
- link AB: A-B 4.
- link PBS: P-B 0.8; P-S 1.6; B-S 2.4.
- link AC: A-C 5.06.
- Slider C is a pin in a slot (what rides it may turn).

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: the cylinder between A and B, which extends and retracts at 0.1 cm/s.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The input runs to a limit and reverses, so every part moves back and forth; one full back-and-forth takes 14.37 s.
- The author placed a background image behind this mechanism as a reference, often a photograph or drawing of the real machine. It is shown once, in the picture's tile 0, where a dashed box marks the part of the image the other tiles show; it is not part of the mechanism.
- Traced points: G (on link EFG), O (on link KILMNO ("Hood")). The author chose to show these paths, so they are probably the outputs this mechanism exists for.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 6 links counting the ground, joined by 7 pin joints (the cylinder that drives it not counted): a six-bar chain of the Stephenson type, because its two three-joint links (link EFG and link HIBJ) are joined only through two-joint links.
- Matches: Stephenson six-bar. Its two three-joint links are not joined directly.
- Also matches: cylinder-driven lever. Cylinder A-B, anchored at A, pushes link HIBJ at B and swings it about its fixed pivot.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots A, E, J (apart: A-E 1.95; A-J 3.28; E-J 1.33).
- link EFG — bell crank (a rocker whose two arms meet at an angle at its pivot), carries traced point G: rocks about ground E through 74.7 deg; it reaches its two ends when cylinder A-B's length is 4.12 and 3.41; its arms to F and G meet at 87 deg at the pivot, so a push on one comes out of the other at that angle.
- link GH — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 38.6 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link HIBJ — beam (a rocker with arms on both sides of its pivot): rocks about ground J through 82.4 deg; it reaches its two ends when cylinder A-B's length is 3.41 and 4.12; the cylinder pushes it at B.
- link FK — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 86.9 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link KILMNO ("Hood") — coupler, carries traced point O: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 67 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- cylinder A-B — driven input (a linear actuator); the block marked P on it is the cylinder's own sliding seal, part of the cylinder and not a separate slider: extends and retracts between lengths 3.41 and 4.12 (travel 0.72).
### How the parts relate
- Four-bar loop: link EFG (E-G) 0.7, link GH (G-H) 0.94, link HIBJ (J-H) 0.67, ground E-J 1.33. It is a non-Grashof (triple-rocker) four-bar: no bar can turn fully relative to the ground (shortest + longest = 2 vs the other two = 1.64).
- The cylinder pushes link HIBJ at B, 0.85 from its pivot J: 0.72 of extension swings it 82.4 deg, about 114.7 deg per unit of extension.
- link HIBJ is a lever (beam) pivoted at J between H and I: they sit on opposite sides of the pivot (arms 0.67 and 3.18), so the two ends always move in opposite directions, and I moves 4.75x as far as H.
- G's path lies overlapping the span of the ground pivots (path x 2.21 to 2.72, y 0.56 to 1.23; pivots x 0.14 to 3.33, y 0.05 to 0.81).
- O's path lies entirely left of every ground pivot (path x -4.49 to -2.95, y -0.03 to 12.96; pivots x 0.14 to 3.33, y 0.05 to 0.81).

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint A turns link AC relative to the ground at 10 rpm counterclockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The input runs to a limit and reverses, so every part moves back and forth; one full back-and-forth takes 2.15 s.
- Traced points: D (on link BCD). The author chose to show these paths, so they are probably the outputs this mechanism exists for.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 4 links counting the ground, joined by 4 pin joints: a single four-bar loop.
- Matches: Chebyshev straight-line linkage. Side links 5 and 5, coupler 2, ground 4: coupler 0.4 and ground 0.8 of the equal side links, traced point D at the coupler's midpoint.
- Also matches: double-rocker four-bar. Grashof, the coupler is shortest: shortest + longest 7 vs the other two 9.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots A, E (apart: A-E 4).
- link AC — input rocker (driven back and forth): rocks about ground A through 64.4 deg.
- link BCD — coupler, carries traced point D: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 212.9 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link BE — rocker: rocks about ground E through 48.9 deg; it reaches its two ends when link AC's angle (A to C) is 37 deg and 90 deg.
### How the parts relate
- Four-bar loop: link AC (A-C) 5, link BCD (C-B) 2, link BE (E-B) 5, ground A-E 4. It is a Grashof double-rocker: the coupler is the shortest bar, so neither side bar can turn fully (shortest + longest = 7 vs the other two = 9).
- D's path lies entirely above every ground pivot (path x -2.35 to 1.81, y 4 to 4.17; pivots x -2 to 2, y 0 to 0).
- D's nearly straight stretch (3.89 long, 85% of the cycle) is the bottom edge of its path; the rest of the path bulges up to 0.17 away from it on one side.
### Paths of moving points
- C: circular arc of radius 5 about A, sweeping 64.4 deg back and forth.
- B: circular arc of radius 5 about E, sweeping 48.9 deg back and forth.
- D (traced): curve traced back and forth, 4.16 wide x 0.17 tall; nearly straight for 85% of the cycle over 3.89 (at 0 deg, deviation within 0.22% of that length).
### The picture: this mechanism at six moments, numbered in time order (1 and 6 are the two ends of its travel)
- 1: 0.81 s, link AC's angle (A to C) 101 deg.
- 2: 1.02 s, link AC's angle (A to C) 89 deg.
- 3: 1.23 s, link AC's angle (A to C) 76 deg.
- 4: 1.45 s, link AC's angle (A to C) 63 deg.
- 5: 1.67 s, link AC's angle (A to C) 50 deg.
- 6: 1.88 s, link AC's angle (A to C) 37 deg.
### Geometry at the start, for reference
- Joints: A (-2, 0) ground; C (1, 4); B (-1, 4); D (0, 4); E (2, 0) ground.
- link AC: A-C 5.
- link BCD: B-C 2; B-D 1; C-D 1.
- link BE: B-E 5.

- link JL — coupler, carries traced point L: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 138.6 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link KL — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 138.7 deg while it moves (general plane motion).

- L's path lies entirely below every ground pivot (path x 5.21 to 16.79, y -3.19 to -3.18; pivots x 11 to 11, y -0.5 to 1.5).

- I: circular arc of radius 2 about H, sweeping 204 deg back and forth.
- J: circular arc of radius 5 about G, sweeping 110.3 deg back and forth.
- K: circular arc of radius 5 about G, sweeping 110.3 deg back and forth.
- L (traced): straight line at 180 deg, length 11.58 (back and forth).

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint A turns link AB relative to the ground at 10 rpm clockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The motion repeats every 6 s, once per input revolution.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 6 links counting the ground, joined by 7 pin joints: a six-bar chain of the Stephenson type, because its two three-joint links (the ground and link BCE) are joined only through two-joint links.
- Matches: Stephenson six-bar. Its two three-joint links are not joined directly.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots A, D, G (apart: A-D 5.49; A-G 8.47; D-G 3.72).
- link AB — input crank: turns full revolutions about ground A, at a steady angular speed.
- link BCE — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 32.1 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link CD — rocker: rocks about ground D through 97.2 deg; it reaches its two ends when link AB's angle (A to B) is 18 deg and 204 deg; one way takes 2.9 s and the other 3.1 s (time ratio 1.07).
- link EF — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 78.2 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link FG — rocker: rocks about ground G through 36.4 deg; it reaches its two ends when link AB's angle (A to B) is 77 deg and 226 deg; one way takes 3.52 s and the other 2.48 s (time ratio 1.42).
### How the parts relate
- Four-bar loop: link AB (A-B) 1.52, link BCE (B-C) 5.59, link CD (D-C) 2.06, ground A-D 5.49. It is a Grashof crank-rocker: link AB (A-B) is the shortest bar, so it is able to turn fully while the opposite side bar only rocks (shortest + longest = 7.1 vs the other two = 7.55).

- C: circular arc of radius 2.06 about D, sweeping 97.2 deg back and forth.
- E: closed curve, 3.08 wide x 2.16 tall, does not cross itself; nearly straight for 16% of the cycle over 1.76 (at 26.3 deg, deviation within 0.44% of that length).
- F: circular arc of radius 5.1 about G, sweeping 36.4 deg back and forth.

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint A turns link AB ("Input lever") relative to the ground at 16 rpm clockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The input runs to a limit and reverses, so every part moves back and forth; one full back-and-forth takes 6.44 s.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 4 links counting the ground, joined by 4 pin joints: a single four-bar loop.
- Matches: triple-rocker four-bar. Non-Grashof: shortest + longest 6.21 vs the other two 6.11.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots A, D (apart: A-D 5).
- link AB ("Input lever") — input crank: turns about ground A through 309 deg and then back the same way, because the input reverses.
- link BC ("Coupler") — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 52.5 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link CDL ("Rocker") — rocker: rocks about ground D through 73.2 deg; it reaches its two ends when link AB ("Input lever")'s angle (A to B) is 30 deg and 205 deg.
### How the parts relate
- Four-bar loop: link AB ("Input lever") (A-B) 1.21, link BC ("Coupler") (B-C) 3.55, link CDL ("Rocker") (D-C) 2.56, ground A-D 5. It is a non-Grashof (triple-rocker) four-bar: no bar can turn fully relative to the ground (shortest + longest = 6.21 vs the other two = 6.11).
### Paths of moving points
- B: circular arc of radius 1.21 about A, sweeping 309 deg back and forth.
- C: circular arc of radius 2.56 about D, sweeping 73.2 deg back and forth.
- L: circular arc of radius 3.04 about D, sweeping 73.2 deg back and forth.
### The picture: this mechanism at six moments, numbered in time order (1 and 6 are the two ends of its travel)
- 1: 1.86 s, link AB ("Input lever")'s angle (A to B) 205 deg.
- 2: 2.51 s, link AB ("Input lever")'s angle (A to B) 267 deg.
- 3: 3.16 s, link AB ("Input lever")'s angle (A to B) 329 deg.
- 4: 3.79 s, link AB ("Input lever")'s angle (A to B) 30 deg.
- 5: 4.44 s, link AB ("Input lever")'s angle (A to B) 92 deg.
- 6: 5.08 s, link AB ("Input lever")'s angle (A to B) 154 deg.
### Loads the author placed
- Force F1 on link CDL ("Rocker") at (5.9, 2.9), magnitude 1.5, pointing at -143 deg.
### Geometry at the start, for reference
- Joints: A (0, 0) ground; B (1.1, 0.5); C (4.1, 2.4); D (5, 0) ground; L (5.9, 2.9).
- link AB ("Input lever"): A-B 1.21.

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint A turns link AB ("Drag crank") relative to the ground at 10 rpm counterclockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The motion repeats every 6 s, once per input revolution.
- Traced points: C (on link BC ("Drag coupler")). The author chose to show these paths, so they are probably the outputs this mechanism exists for.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 4 links counting the ground, joined by 4 pin joints: a single four-bar loop.
- Matches: double-crank (drag-link) four-bar. Grashof, the ground is shortest: shortest + longest 3.5 vs the other two 4.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots A, D (apart: A-D 1).
- link AB ("Drag crank") — input crank: turns full revolutions about ground A, at a steady angular speed.
- link BC ("Drag coupler") — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it turns full revolutions while it moves (general plane motion).
- link CD ("Drag output") — crank, carries traced point C: turns full revolutions about ground D, unevenly: its angular speed ranges from 27.3 to 131.9 deg/s (fastest/slowest 4.84).
### How the parts relate
- Four-bar loop: link AB ("Drag crank") (A-B) 2, link BC ("Drag coupler") (B-C) 2.5, link CD ("Drag output") (D-C) 2, ground A-D 1. It is a Grashof double-crank (drag link): the ground is the shortest bar, so both side bars are able to turn fully (shortest + longest = 3.5 vs the other two = 4).
- C's path lies overlapping the span of the ground pivots (path x -1 to 3, y -2 to 2; pivots x 0 to 1, y 0 to 0).
### Paths of moving points
- B: full circle of radius 2 about A.
- C (traced): full circle of radius 2 about D.

## Mechanism M2
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint E turns link EF ("Crank") relative to the ground at 8 rpm clockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The motion repeats every 7.5 s, once per input revolution.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 3 links counting the ground, joined by 2 pin joints and 1 sliding joint.
- Matches: in-line slider-crank. Link EF ("Crank") turns fully and drives slider G along a fixed guide through connecting rod link FG ("Connecting rod").
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots E.
- link EF ("Crank") — input crank: turns full revolutions about ground E, at a steady angular speed.
- link FG ("Connecting rod") — connecting rod: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 38.9 deg while it moves (general plane motion).

### How the parts relate
- Slider-crank: link EF ("Crank") (radius 1 about E) drives slider G through rod link FG ("Connecting rod") (length 3, 3x the crank radius). The guide is in line with the crank pivot, so the two strokes are symmetric.
### Paths of moving points

- G: straight line at 0 deg, length 2 (back and forth).

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint O turns link OAR relative to the ground at 10 rpm counterclockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The motion repeats every 6 s, once per input revolution.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 5 links counting the ground, joined by 5 pin joints and 1 sliding joint.
- Matches: steam-locomotive running gear (driving wheels, side rod and main rod). Link OAR and link PBS are wheels (drawn as discs) tied by side rod link AB, which keeps its angle, so they turn together; link AC joins them to slider C on a fixed guide, as a main rod joins a piston's crosshead to a driving wheel.
- Also matches: in-line slider-crank. Link OAR turns fully and drives slider C along a fixed guide through connecting rod link AC.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots O, P (apart: O-P 4).
- link OAR — input crank, drawn by its author as a disc (a wheel or flywheel): turns full revolutions about ground O, at a steady angular speed.
- link AB — side rod (a coupling rod): ties link OAR and link PBS to turn together; moves along a curve without turning: not in a straight line; every point of it traces the same circular arc as A (radius 0.8 about O), shifted (curvilinear translation).
- link PBS — crank, drawn by its author as a disc (a wheel or flywheel): turns full revolutions about ground P, at a steady angular speed.
- link AC — connecting rod: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 18.2 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- slider C — slider on a fixed guide: travels 1.6 back and forth along a fixed guide at 0 deg; it reaches its two ends when link OAR's angle (O to R) is 0 deg and 180 deg; one way takes 3 s and the other 3 s (time ratio 1).

- Four-bar loop: link OAR (O-A) 0.8, link AB (A-B) 4, link PBS (P-B) 0.8, ground O-P 4. It is a parallelogram: opposite bars are equal and the coupler keeps its angle, so the coupler stays parallel to the ground line and the two side bars stay parallel to each other.
- Slider-crank: link OAR (radius 0.8 about O) drives slider C through rod link AC (length 5.06, 6.33x the crank radius). The guide is in line with the crank pivot, so the two strokes are symmetric.
- link OAR and link PBS turn together: their angles change identically at every instant (both sweep 360 deg), so the angle between them never changes. Line O-R stays parallel to line P-S.

- A: full circle of radius 0.8 about O.
- R: full circle of radius 1.6 about O.
- B: full circle of radius 0.8 about P.
- S: full circle of radius 1.6 about P.
- C: straight line at 0 deg, length 1.6 (back and forth).

answer.plainEnglish: This mechanism contains four separate assemblies. Driven **AB** turns, and **BC** transfers its motion to **slider C**, which travels 2.4 cm back and forth. **FG** moves **pin G** along the slot in **EH**, making **EH** turn unevenly; **EF** stays fixed. **JK** moves **pin K** along the slot in **MN**, making **MN** rock with a slower swing and a faster return; **JM** stays fixed. Driven **PQ** rocks instead of turning fully, and **QR** transfers that motion to **slider R**. Together, these show different ways to transfer motion.

useCases.why: The assembly with **AB**, **BC** and **slider C** converts continuous rotation into straight back-and-forth travel suitable for moving a piston.
The assembly with **JK** and **MN** provides unequal swing times, allowing a slower cutting stroke and a faster return through an attached tool drive.

- Matches: steam-locomotive running gear (driving wheels, side rod and main rod). Link OAR and link PBS are wheels (drawn as discs) tied by side rod link AB, which keeps its angle, so they turn together; link AC joins them to slider C on a fixed guide, as a main rod joins a piston's crosshead to a driving wheel.
- Also matches: in-line slider-crank. Link OAR turns fully and drives slider C along a fixed guide through connecting rod link AC.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots O, P (apart: O-P 4).

- link AB — side rod (a coupling rod): ties link OAR and link PBS to turn together; moves along a curve without turning: not in a straight line; every point of it traces the same circular arc as A (radius 0.8 about O), shifted (curvilinear translation).
- link PBS — crank, drawn by its author as a disc (a wheel or flywheel): turns full revolutions about ground P, at a steady angular speed.
- link AC — connecting rod: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 18.2 deg while it moves (general plane motion).

- link OAR and link PBS turn together: their angles change identically at every instant (both sweep 360 deg), so the angle between them never changes. Line O-R stays parallel to line P-S.

answer.plainEnglish: This mechanism is two identical legs, each driven by its own input crank, **AB** and **IJ**, at 10 rpm, with the cranks set half a turn apart. In each leg the crank drives two four-bar loops at once: one rocks the bell crank **CDE**, the other rocks **CF**. Couplers **EG** and **FGH** combine these swings so **H** traces a closed loop whose bottom edge is nearly straight for 40.37 cm, 28% of the cycle, like a foot pressing along flat ground. **P** repeats this, half a cycle later.
answer.resembles: Two-legged crank-driven walking machine, legs out of step

useCases.why: One steadily turning crank per leg makes the foot point run along a nearly straight bottom edge, so the kit walks with a single motor and no leg control.
Legs set half a cycle apart take turns on the ground, so one continuous rotation keeps the body supported while it walks.

### At a glance
- Driven input: joint A turns link AB relative to the ground at 10 rpm counterclockwise.

- link BD — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 46.3 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link CDE — bell crank (a rocker whose two arms meet at an angle at its pivot): rocks about ground C through 56.5 deg; it reaches its two ends when link AB's angle (A to B) is 303 deg and 154 deg; one way takes 3.52 s and the other 2.48 s (time ratio 1.42); its arms to D and E meet at 86 deg at the pivot, so a push on one comes out of the other at that angle.

- link CF — rocker: rocks about ground C through 86.1 deg; it reaches its two ends when link AB's angle (A to B) is 202 deg and 65 deg; one way takes 3.72 s and the other 2.28 s (time ratio 1.63).
- link EG — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 81.3 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link FGH — coupler, carries traced point H: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 64.5 deg while it moves (general plane motion).

- Four-bar loop: link AB (A-B) 15, link BD (B-D) 50, link CDE (C-D) 41.5, ground A-C 38.79. It is a Grashof crank-rocker: link AB (A-B) is the shortest bar, so it is able to turn fully while the opposite side bar only rocks (shortest + longest = 65 vs the other two = 80.29).

answer.plainEnglish: This mechanism appears in three separate copies. The driven beams **CDE**, **JKL** and **QRS** rock about fixed pivots **D**, **K** and **R**, with their ends moving in opposite directions. Couplers **BC**, **IJ** and **PQ** connect one end of each beam to rockers **AB**, **HI** and **OP**, which swing about the frame. At the other ends, connecting rods **EF**, **LM** and **ST** move **slider F**, **slider M** and **slider T** up and down through 2.09 cm along fixed vertical guides.

useCases.why: A beam rocking about a fixed pivot transfers motion between opposite ends to raise and lower a pump rod.

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint C turns link CDE relative to link BC at 10 rpm counterclockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The input runs to a limit and reverses, so every part moves back and forth; one full back-and-forth takes 2 s.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 5 links counting the ground, joined by 5 pin joints and 1 sliding joint.
- Matches: walking-beam mechanism. Link CDE is a beam rocking about a pivot between its ends; one end (C) is moved by the rest of the mechanism, the other (E) works slider F up and down a fixed guide through rod link EF.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots A, D (apart: A-D 4.2).
- link AB — rocker: rocks about ground A through 155.2 deg; it reaches its two ends when link CDE's angle (C to E) is 21 deg and 345 deg.
- link BC — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 28.5 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link CDE — input rocker (driven back and forth): rocks about ground D through 37.8 deg.
- link EF — connecting rod: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 5.3 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- slider F — slider on a fixed guide: travels 2.09 back and forth along a fixed guide at 90 deg; it reaches its two ends when link CDE's angle (C to E) is 345 deg and 22 deg.
### How the parts relate
- Four-bar loop: link AB (A-B) 1, link BC (B-C) 3.3, link CDE (D-C) 2.5, ground A-D 4.2. It is a Grashof crank-rocker: link AB (A-B) is the shortest bar, so it is able to turn fully while the opposite side bar only rocks (shortest + longest = 5.2 vs the other two = 5.8). In this mechanism it does not turn fully: it sweeps 155.2 deg over the solved motion.
- Slider-crank arrangement driven by a rocking lever: link CDE (arm 3.2 from its pivot D, swinging 37.8 deg) pushes slider F along its guide through rod link EF (length 2.6).
- link CDE is a lever (beam) pivoted at D between C and E: they sit on opposite sides of the pivot (arms 2.5 and 3.2), so the two ends always move in opposite directions, and E moves 1.28x as far as C.
### Paths of moving points
- B: circular arc of radius 1 about A, sweeping 155.2 deg back and forth.
- C: circular arc of radius 2.5 about D, sweeping 37.8 deg back and forth.
- E: circular arc of radius 3.2 about D, sweeping 37.8 deg back and forth.
- F: straight line at 90 deg, length 2.09 (back and forth).

answer.plainEnglish: The input **AB** turns full circles about **A** at 10 rpm clockwise. Through the coupler **BC**, each turn rocks the bell crank **CDE** back and forth through 61 deg about **D**. The arm of **CDE** that reaches **E** sits at 90 deg to its other arm, and it passes the rocking on through the coupler **EF** to the rocker **FG**. **FG** then swings through 42.3 deg about **G**. Two four-bar loops share **CDE**: the first turns rotation into rocking, and the second relays that rocking. The output swing is uneven: **FG** swings one way in 2.42 s and returns in 3.58 s.

A bell crank passes a rocking motion around a corner to a distant pivot, as **CDE** does at 90 deg to drive **FG**.

answer.plainEnglish: This mechanism contains three separate moving systems. Driven **AB** turns **BC**, which carries motion to **CD**; **CD** completes full turns while speeding up and slowing down, and **C** traces a circle of radius 2 cm. Driven **EF** pushes and pulls through **FG**, moving **slider G** along a straight guide with equal times for the outward and return strokes. The arrangement of **HI**, **IJ**, and **JK** converts continuous rotation into a limited back-and-forth swing suitable for sweeping a wiper.

- Structure: 4 links counting the ground, joined by 4 pin joints: a single four-bar loop.
- Matches: crank-rocker four-bar. Grashof, link GK ("Luffing crank") is shortest: shortest + longest 4.3 vs the other two 5.13.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots G, O (apart: G-O 2.53).
- link GK ("Luffing crank") — input crank: turns full revolutions about ground G, at a steady angular speed.
- link CK ("Luffing link") — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 65.6 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link OCT ("Jib") — rocker: rocks about ground O through 52.2 deg; it reaches its two ends when link GK ("Luffing crank")'s angle (G to K) is 240 deg and 104 deg; one way takes 4.15 s and the other 2.52 s (time ratio 1.65).

- K: full circle of radius 1.1 about G.
- C: circular arc of radius 3.2 about O, sweeping 52.2 deg back and forth.
- T: circular arc of radius 7 about O, sweeping 52.2 deg back and forth.

answer.plainEnglish: This mechanism is two identical legs, each driven by its own input crank, **AB** and **IJ**, at 10 rpm, with the cranks set half a turn apart. In each leg the crank drives two four-bar loops at once: one rocks the bell crank **CDE**, the other rocks **CF**. Couplers **EG** and **FGH** combine these swings so **H** traces a closed loop whose bottom edge is nearly straight for 40.37 cm, 28% of the cycle, like a foot pressing along flat ground. **P** repeats this, half a cycle later.

### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots A, C (apart: A-C 38.79).
- link AB — input crank: turns full revolutions about ground A, at a steady angular speed.
- link BD — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 46.3 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link CDE — bell crank (a rocker whose two arms meet at an angle at its pivot): rocks about ground C through 56.5 deg; it reaches its two ends when link AB's angle (A to B) is 303 deg and 154 deg; one way takes 3.52 s and the other 2.48 s (time ratio 1.42); its arms to D and E meet at 86 deg at the pivot, so a push on one comes out of the other at that angle.
- link BF — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 51.4 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link CF — rocker: rocks about ground C through 86.1 deg; it reaches its two ends when link AB's angle (A to B) is 202 deg and 65 deg; one way takes 3.72 s and the other 2.28 s (time ratio 1.63).
- link EG — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 81.3 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link FGH — coupler, carries traced point H: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 64.5 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
### How the parts relate
- Four-bar loop: link AB (A-B) 15, link BD (B-D) 50, link CDE (C-D) 41.5, ground A-C 38.79. It is a Grashof crank-rocker: link AB (A-B) is the shortest bar, so it is able to turn fully while the opposite side bar only rocks (shortest + longest = 65 vs the other two = 80.29).
- Four-bar loop: link AB (A-B) 15, link BF (B-F) 61.9, link CF (C-F) 39.3, ground A-C 38.79. It is a Grashof crank-rocker: link AB (A-B) is the shortest bar, so it is able to turn fully while the opposite side bar only rocks (shortest + longest = 76.9 vs the other two = 78.09).
- H's path lies entirely below every ground pivot (path x -71.52 to -3.61, y -91.83 to -69.38; pivots x -38 to 0, y -7.8 to 0).
- H's nearly straight stretch (40.37 long, 28% of the cycle) is the bottom edge of its path; the rest of the path bulges up to 22.52 away from it on one side.
### Paths of moving points
- B: full circle of radius 15 about A.
- D: circular arc of radius 41.5 about C, sweeping 56.5 deg back and forth.
- E: circular arc of radius 40.1 about C, sweeping 56.5 deg back and forth.

- G: closed curve, 51.11 wide x 38.53 tall, does not cross itself; nearly straight for 22% of the cycle over 27.25 (at 177.4 deg, deviation within 0.45% of that length).
- H (traced): closed curve, 67.91 wide x 22.45 tall, does not cross itself; nearly straight for 28% of the cycle over 40.37 (at 0.3 deg, deviation within 0.5% of that length).

answer.plainEnglish: This mechanism appears three times side by side. The copies are identical except for speed: 10, 8 and 12 rpm, giving cycles of 2 s, 2.5 s and 1.67 s. In the first copy the input at **C** rocks beam **CDE** through 37.8 deg about **D**, like a seesaw. Its far end **E** drives rod **EF**, pushing **slider F** 2.09 cm up and down its guide. On the near side, coupler **BC** swings rocker **AB** back and forth. **AB** is short enough to turn fully but never does.
